Operating results for the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">six</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">June&#160;30, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> are not necessarily indicative of the results that may be expected for the year ending </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">. As discussed in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Note&#160;2</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the outbreak of COVID-19 and its development into a pandemic in March 2020 resulted in significant economic disruption globally. This disruption became more acute in the latter half of March 2020. While demand and market prices for most of our products increased during the second quarter of 2020 compared to the end of the first quarter of 2020, developments with respect to COVID-19 have been occurring at a rapid pace and the risk remains that circumstances could change. For instance, during the latter part of the second quarter of 2020, governmental authorities in various states across the U.S. began to lift many of the restrictions created by actions taken to slow down the spread of COVID-19. However, many of the states where such restrictions were lifted, and several states where the restrictions have essentially never been lifted (such as California in our U.S. West Coast region), have recently experienced a marked increase in the spread of COVID-19 and many governmental authorities in such areas have responded by reimposing certain restrictions they had previously lifted. Therefore, our operating results for the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">six</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">June&#160;30, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> do not fully reflect the impact this disruption will likely continue to have on us.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The balance sheet as of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> has been derived from our audited financial statements as of that date. We reduced the amount of crude oil processed at most of our refineries in response to the decreased demand for our products, we temporarily idled various gasoline-making units at certain of our refineries to further limit gasoline production, and we took measures to reduce jet fuel production. </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span><ix:nonFraction id="d10901957e590-wk-Fact-157011CC3F47EC3D43D828B713247807" name="vlo:NumberOfEthanolPlantsTemporarilyIdled" contextRef="D2020Q1Mar01-Mar31" unitRef="plant" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">Eight</ix:nonFraction></span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of our ethanol plants were temporarily idled, and production at our remaining </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span><ix:nonFraction id="d10901957e594-wk-Fact-AADDF148A445B726C96328B71324CA7D" name="vlo:NumberOfEthanolPlantsWithTemporarilyReducedProduction" contextRef="D2020Q1Mar01-Mar31" unitRef="plant" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">six</ix:nonFraction></span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#160;ethanol plants was reduced earlier this year to address the decreased demand for ethanol. We believe we have proactively addressed many of the known impacts of COVID-19 to the extent possible and we will strive to continue to do so, but there can be no assurance that any measures we have taken or may take will be fully effective. As a result, we expect these matters may affect our estimates and assumptions on amounts reported in the financial statements and accompanying notes in the near style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Due to the adverse economic conditions discussed above, we reviewed our significant Based on our analysis, we determined that the carrying amount of each of these plants was recoverable, as the undiscounted future cash flows from each plant exceeded its respective carrying value. Nonetheless, we will continue to evaluate the economic conditions and their impact on our assumptions.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Impairment Analysis of Goodwill</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We have </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$<ix:nonFraction id="d10901957e627-wk-Fact-2A28D3C139C48300403228B71324AB2A" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="FI2020Q2" unitRef="usd" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">260</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of goodwill as of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">June&#160;30, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">. value of inventories to their cost on an aggregate basis, excluding materials and supplies. In determining the market value of our inventories, we assume that feedstocks are converted into refined products, which requires us to make estimates regarding the refined products expected to be produced from those feedstocks and the conversion costs required to convert those feedstocks into refined products. We also estimate the usual and customary transportation costs required to move the inventory from our plants to the appropriate points of sale. We then apply an estimated selling price to our inventories. If the aggregate market value is less than the aggregate cost, we recognize a loss for the difference in our statements of income. To the extent the aggregate market value subsequently increases, we would recognize an increase to the value of our inventories (not to exceed cost) and a gain in our statements of income.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The market value of our last-in, first-out (LIFO) inventory fell below our historical LIFO inventory costs as of March&#160;31, 2020, and as a result, we recorded an LCM inventory valuation reserve of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$<ix:nonFraction id="d10902635e1010-wk-Fact-1E6E72AFB29A5155ECD5B9473BB9031C" name="us-gaap:InventoryValuationReserves" contextRef="FI2020Q1" unitRef="usd" decimals="-8" scale="9" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">2.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in order to state our inventories at market. Some of these contracts are derivative instruments; however, we elect the normal purchase exception and do not record these contracts at their fair values. Certain of these programs require us to blend biofuels into the products we produce, and we are subject to such programs in most of the countries in which we operate. These countries set annual quotas for the percentage of biofuels that must be blended into the motor fuels consumed in these countries. As a producer of motor fuels from petroleum, we are obligated to blend biofuels into the products we produce at a rate that is at least equal to the applicable quota. These non-GAAP financial measures include adjusted operating income (including adjusted operating income for each of our reportable segments, as applicable) and refining, renewable diesel, and ethanol segment margin. We have included these non-GAAP financial measures to help facilitate the comparison of operating results between periods. See the tables in note&#160;(d) beginning on page&#160;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;text-align:right;vertical-align:bottom;">57</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> for reconciliations of these non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable U.S. GAAP financial measures. Also in note</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#ff0000;font-weight:bold;">&#160;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">(d), we disclose the reasons why we believe our use of the non-GAAP financial measures provides useful information.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div><a id="s786382ECB6385E8BB5FE1E777E14173A"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">OVERVIEW AND OUTLOOK</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div><a id="s52F7D00174325BD29D6A86533E0F8831"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Overview</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;padding-left:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Business Operations Update</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The outbreak of COVID-19 and its development into a pandemic in March 2020 has resulted in significant economic disruption globally, including in North America and Europe, the primary geographic areas where we operate. In March, governmental authorities around the world took actions, such as stay-at-home orders and other social distancing measures, to slow down the spread of COVID-19 that restricted travel, public gatherings, and the overall level of individual movement and in-person interaction across the globe. These actions have significantly reduced global economic activity and negatively impacted many businesses, including our business. Airlines have dramatically reduced flights and motor vehicle usage has significantly declined at a time when seasonal driving patterns typically result in an increase of consumer demand for gasoline. As a result, there has also been a decline in the demand for, and thus also the market prices of, crude oil and most of our products. In addition, global crude oil production levels did not decline initially despite lower demand and storage capacity constraints for crude oil and refined products, which, during March 2020 and much of the second quarter of 2020, exacerbated the decline in crude oil prices and contributed to an increase in crude oil price volatility.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">During the latter part of the second quarter of 2020, governmental authorities in various states across the U.S., particularly those in our U.S. Gulf Coast and U.S. Mid-Continent regions, began to lift many of the restrictions created by actions taken to slow down the spread of COVID-19, while many governmental authorities in our U.S. West Coast and North Atlantic regions only recently began taking similar actions. These actions have resulted in an increase in the level of individual movement and travel and, in turn, an increase in the demand and market prices for most of our products relative to late March 2020. However, many of the states where such restrictions were lifted, and several states where the restrictions have essentially never been lifted (such as California in our U.S. West Coast region), have recently experienced a marked increase in the spread of COVID-19 and many governmental authorities in such areas have responded by reimposing certain restrictions they had previously lifted. While this response has not yet significantly impacted the increased level of individual movement associated with the initial lifting of many restrictions, the risk remains that the reimposition of such restrictions that has already occurred, or any further reimposition </span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">40</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:8pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;color:#0000ff;" href="#s17D2117B79315F2B914A0F26C91DE312"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;color:#0000ff;">Table of Contents</span></a></div></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">of prior restrictions or any imposition of new restrictions that may occur in the future, could each weaken the partial recovery in the demand and market prices for our products, which would negatively affect us.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The decrease in the demand for refined petroleum products coupled with the decline in the price of crude oil has resulted in a significant decrease in the price of refined petroleum products manufactured by our refining segment. For example, the price of gasoline</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:7pt">(a)</sup></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in the U.S. Gulf Coast region where eight of our 15&#160;refineries are located was $68.82&#160;per barrel at the beginning of 2020, fell to $17.65&#160;per barrel at the end of March (a 74&#160;percent decline), and partially recovered to $46.58&#160;per barrel by the end of June (a 32&#160;percent decline over the six-month period). Another example is the price of diesel</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:7pt">(b)</sup></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in the U.S. Gulf Coast region, which was $81.71&#160;per barrel at the beginning of 2020, fell to $39.18&#160;per barrel at the end of March (a 52&#160;percent decline), and partially recovered to $47.58&#160;per barrel by the end of June (a 42&#160;percent decline over the six-month period). On July&#160;29, 2020, the prices of gasoline</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:7pt">(a)</sup></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and diesel</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:7pt">(b)</sup></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> were $46.44&#160;per barrel and $50.76&#160;per barrel, respectively.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The price of ethanol manufactured by our ethanol segment has also decreased due to a decline in demand. Because ethanol is primarily blended into gasoline, ethanol demand declined along with the decline in the demand for gasoline. Demand for renewable diesel, however, has not significantly declined due to continued demand for this low-carbon fuel despite the current economic environment; therefore, our renewable diesel segment has not been impacted as significantly as our refining and ethanol segments.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Prices for the products we sell and the feedstocks we purchase impact our revenues, cost of sales, operating income, and liquidity. In addition, a decline in the market prices of products and feedstocks below their carrying values in our inventory results in a writedown in the value of our inventories, and a subsequent recovery in market prices results in a write-up in the value of our inventories to their previous carrying values. These inventory valuation adjustments are referred to as &#8220;lower of cost or market (LCM) inventory valuation adjustments&#8221; and are described in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Note&#160;4</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of Condensed Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements. For the second quarter of 2020, we generated operating income of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$1.8&#160;billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, which includes a </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$2.2&#160;billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> recovery in the value of our inventories. We wrote down the value of our inventories by $2.5&#160;billion in the first quarter of 2020 due to the significant decline in market prices at that time, but as previously noted, market prices improved during the second quarter resulting in the reversal of all but </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$294&#160;million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of the initial writedown. For the first six months of 2020, we generated an operating loss of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$488&#160;million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, which includes the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$294&#160;million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> writedown in the value of our inventories. Our operating results for the second quarter and the first six months of 2020, including operating results by segment, are described in the summary below and detailed descriptions can be found under &#8220;RESULTS OF OPERATIONS&#8221; on pages&#160;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">45</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;text-align:right;vertical-align:bottom;"> </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">through&#160;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">65</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Our cash and cash equivalents declined by </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$264&#160;million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> during the first six months of 2020, from </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$2.6&#160;billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> as of December&#160;31, 2019 to </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$2.3&#160;billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> as of June&#160;30, 2020. We invested </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$1.3&#160;billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in our business and returned </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;text-align:right;vertical-align:bottom;">$948&#160;million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> to our stockholders primarily through dividends, but also through purchases of our common stock, which, as discussed below, have not occurred under our stock purchase program since mid-March 2020. These uses of cash were largely offset by proceeds from a $1.5&#160;billion public debt offering completed in April 2020 as described in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Note&#160;6</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of Condensed Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements. In addition, our operations generated net cash of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$687&#160;million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, which was driven by a decrease in inventory on hand. Even though our cash and cash equivalents on hand declined during the first six months of 2020, we ended the period with </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$7.7&#160;billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of liquidity</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:7pt">(c)</sup></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">. We reduced the amount of crude oil processed at most of our refineries in response to the decreased demand for our products, we temporarily idled various gasoline-making units at certain of our refineries to further limit gasoline production, and we took measures to reduce jet fuel production. Eight of our ethanol plants were temporarily idled, and production at our remaining six ethanol plants was reduced earlier this year to address the decreased demand for ethanol. Demand for most of our products partially recovered during the latter part of the second quarter of 2020. As a result, we have increased the production of most of our products and recently restarted the gasoline-making units and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">four</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> ethanol plants that had been temporarily idled. The market prices for refined petroleum products generally track the price of benchmark crude oils, such as Brent, WTI, and ANS; therefore, our refining segment margin is affected by our ability to purchase and process crude oils and other feedstocks that are priced at a discount to the benchmark crude oils. While we benefit when we process these types of crude oils and other feedstocks, that benefit will vary as the discount increases or decreases. Increases in these discounts have a favorable impact on our refining segment margin as it lowers our cost of materials; whereas lower discounts result in higher cost of materials, which has a negative impact on our refining segment margin. A long-lived asset is not recoverable if its carrying amount exceeds the sum of the undiscounted cash flows expected to result from its use and eventual disposition. If a long-lived asset is not recoverable, an impairment loss is recognized for the amount by which </span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">69</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:8pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;color:#0000ff;" href="#s17D2117B79315F2B914A0F26C91DE312"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;color:#0000ff;">Table of Contents</span></a></div></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:14px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">the carrying amount of the long-lived asset exceeds its fair value, with fair value determined based on discounted estimated net cash flows or other appropriate methods.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Goodwill is tested for impairment annually or more frequently if events or changes in circumstances indicate the asset might be impaired. This disruption became more acute in the latter half of March 2020. While demand and market prices for most of our products increased during the second quarter of 2020 compared to the end of the first quarter of 2020, developments with respect to COVID-19 have been occurring at a rapid pace and the risk remains that circumstances could change. For instance, during the latter part of the second quarter of 2020, governmental authorities in various states across the U.S. began to lift many of the restrictions created by actions taken to slow down the spread of COVID-19. However, many of the states where such restrictions were lifted, and several states where the restrictions have essentially never been lifted (such as California in our U.S. West Coast region), have recently experienced a marked increase in the spread of COVID-19 and many governmental authorities in such areas have responded by reimposing certain restrictions they had previously lifted. Therefore, our operating results for the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; do not fully reflect the impact this disruption will likely continue to have on us.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;The balance sheet as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;December&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; has been derived from our audited financial statements as of that date. This disruption became more acute in the latter half of March 2020. While demand and market prices for most of our products increased during the second quarter of 2020 compared to the end of the first quarter of 2020, developments with respect to COVID-19 have been occurring at a rapid pace and the risk remains that circumstances could change. For instance, during the latter part of the second quarter of 2020, governmental authorities in various states across the U.S. began to lift many of the restrictions created by actions taken to slow down the spread of COVID-19. However, many of the states where such restrictions were lifted, and several states where the restrictions have essentially never been lifted (such as California in our U.S. West Coast region), have recently experienced a marked increase in the spread of COVID-19 and many governmental authorities in such areas have responded by reimposing certain restrictions they had previously lifted.     <us-gaap:UnusualOrInfrequentItemsDisclosureTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2020Q2YTD"
      id="TextSelection-196F4481C5C77F264E1C28B7144372F7-0-wk-Fact-65312EF17F41F1A3AA3E28B7132458F3">&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;2.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;UNCERTAINTIES AND CERTAIN SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Overview&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:14px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;The outbreak of COVID-19 and its development into a pandemic in March&#160;2020 and certain developments in the global oil markets have impacted and continue to impact our business. We responded, and will strive to continue to respond, to the impact from these matters on our business. We reduced the amount of crude oil processed at most of our refineries in response to the decreased demand for our products, we temporarily idled various gasoline-making units at certain of our refineries to further limit gasoline production, and we took measures to reduce jet fuel production. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;Eight&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; of our ethanol plants were temporarily idled, and production at our remaining &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;ethanol plants was reduced earlier this year to address the decreased demand for ethanol. Demand for most of our products partially recovered during the latter part of the second quarter of 2020. As a result, we have increased the production of most of our products and recently restarted the gasoline-making units and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;four&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; ethanol plants that had been temporarily idled.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:14px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Many uncertainties remain with respect to COVID-19, including its resulting economic effects, and we are unable to predict the ultimate economic impacts from COVID-19 on our business and how quickly national economies can recover once the pandemic subsides, or whether any recovery will ultimately experience a reversal or other setbacks. However, the adverse impacts of the economic effects from COVID-19 and uncertainty in the global oil markets on our business have been and will likely continue to be significant. We believe we have proactively addressed many of the known impacts of COVID-19 to the extent possible and we will strive to continue to do so, but there can be no assurance that any measures we have taken or may take will be fully effective. As a result, we expect these matters may affect our estimates and assumptions on amounts reported in the financial statements and accompanying notes in the near term.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Impairment Analysis of Long-Lived Assets&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Due to the adverse economic conditions discussed above, we reviewed our significant operating assets for the existence of impairment indicators. As a result of this review, we evaluated &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;ethanol plants for potential impairment as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, assuming that we would operate these plants in the future and considering current economic conditions on our future estimated cash flows. Based on our analysis, we determined that the carrying amount of each of these plants was recoverable, as the undiscounted future cash flows from each plant exceeded its respective carrying value. Nonetheless, we will continue to evaluate the economic conditions and their impact on our assumptions.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Impairment Analysis of Goodwill&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We have &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$260&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; of goodwill as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;. All of our goodwill is allocated to one reporting unit, the U.S. Gulf Coast refining region. Our annual test for the impairment of goodwill is performed on October&#160;1 of each year. However, as discussed above, there were adverse changes in the capital and commodity markets that contributed to a significant decline in our common stock price compared to the price as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;December&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and early &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;March 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;. Despite the decline in our common stock price, we determined our goodwill was &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;no&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;t impaired as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;. Nonetheless, we will continue to evaluate the economic conditions and their impact on our assumptions.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Inventory Valuation&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;See &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; regarding our &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$294&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; LCM inventory valuation reserve and the estimates used to determine the market value of our inventories.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:UnusualOrInfrequentItemsDisclosureTextBlock>

      id="TextSelection-C509054C1FB54D0FECDA28B71443420E-0-wk-Fact-429DDBE12CF5196D6AA528B7136EA32E">&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;3.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;MERGER WITH VLP&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;On January&#160;10, 2019, we completed our acquisition of all of the outstanding publicly held common units of VLP pursuant to a definitive Agreement and Plan of Merger (Merger Agreement, and together with the transactions contemplated thereby, the Merger Transaction) with VLP. Upon completion of the Merger Transaction, each outstanding publicly held common unit was converted into the right to receive &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$42.25&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;per common unit in cash without any interest thereon, and all such publicly traded common units were automatically canceled and ceased to exist. Upon completion of the Merger Transaction, we paid aggregate merger consideration of&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#ee2724;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$950&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, which was funded with available cash on hand.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Prior to the completion of the Merger Transaction, we consolidated the financial statements of VLP and reflected noncontrolling interests on our balance sheet for the portion of VLP&#x2019;s partners&#x2019; capital held by VLP&#x2019;s public common unitholders. Upon completion of the Merger Transaction, VLP became our indirect wholly owned subsidiary and, as a result, we no longer reflect noncontrolling interests on our balance sheet with respect to VLP. In addition, we no longer attribute a portion of VLP&#x2019;s net income to noncontrolling interests. Because we had a controlling financial interest in VLP before the Merger Transaction and retained our controlling financial interest in VLP after the Merger Transaction, the change in our ownership interest in VLP as a result of the merger was accounted for as an equity transaction. Accordingly, we did not recognize a gain or loss on the Merger Transaction.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:BusinessCombinationDisclosureTextBlock>

solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We compare the market value of inventories to their cost on an aggregate basis, excluding materials and supplies. In determining the market value of our inventories, we assume that feedstocks are converted into refined products, which requires us to make estimates regarding the refined products expected to be produced from those feedstocks and the conversion costs required to convert those feedstocks into refined products. We also estimate the usual and customary transportation costs required to move the inventory from our plants to the appropriate points of sale. We then apply an estimated selling price to our inventories. If the aggregate market value is less than the aggregate cost, we recognize a loss for the difference in our statements of income. To the extent the aggregate market value subsequently increases, we would recognize an increase to the value of our inventories (not to exceed cost) and a gain in our statements of income.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;The market value of our last-in, first-out (LIFO) inventory fell below our historical LIFO inventory costs as of March&#160;31, 2020, and as a result, we recorded an LCM inventory valuation reserve of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$2.5&#160;billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; in order to state our inventories at market. As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, our LCM inventory valuation reserve was &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$294&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;. The change in our LCM inventory valuation reserve resulted in a net benefit of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$2.2&#160;billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#ee2724;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;and a net charge of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$294&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; to our results of operations during the three and six months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, respectively. As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;December&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, the replacement cost (market value) of LIFO inventories exceeded their LIFO carrying amounts by &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$2.5&#160;billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Our non-LIFO inventories accounted for &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$912&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$1.4&#160;billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; of our total inventories as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;December&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, respectively.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:InventoryDisclosureTextBlock>

364-Day Credit Agreement (the 364-day Revolving Credit Facility) with several lenders. This facility provides for a revolving credit facility in an aggregate principal amount of up to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$875&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and matures &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;364&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;days from April&#160;13, 2020.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Borrowings under this facility bear interest at the base rate or the eurodollar rate (at our election) plus an applicable rate ranging from &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;0.150&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;percent to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;1.700&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;percent, based upon the elected interest rate type and our debt ratings from certain rating agencies. The facility requires us to pay a commitment fee accruing on the daily amount of used and unused commitments of the lenders, also based upon our debt ratings mentioned &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;above. The interest and commitment fees under this facility are payable quarterly. The facility also requires us to pay a customary agency fee to the administrative agent. The facility contains various customary covenants and events of default.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Accounts Receivable Sales Facility&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;During the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, we sold &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$300&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; of eligible receivables under our accounts receivable sales facility and repaid &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$400&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;. The most significant changes affecting us were as follows:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Modification of the limitations previously set by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 by providing that tax net operating losses (NOLs) arising in a tax year beginning in 2018, 2019, or 2020 can be carried back five years. In addition, the CARES Act removed the taxable income limitation to allow a tax NOL to fully offset taxable income for tax years beginning before January&#160;1, 2021.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Increased the deductibility of interest expense from &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;30&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;percent to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;50&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;percent of adjusted taxable income for 2019 and 2020. We do not disclose remaining performance obligations for contracts that have terms of one year or less. The transaction price for our remaining term contracts includes a fixed component and variable consideration (i.e., a commodity price), both of which are allocated entirely to a wholly unsatisfied promise to transfer a distinct good that forms part of a single performance obligation. The fixed component is not material and the variable consideration is highly uncertain. Therefore, as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, we have not disclosed the aggregate amount of the transaction price allocated to our remaining performance obligations.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:30px;text-indent:-30px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:30px;text-indent:-30px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Segment Information&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We have &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;reportable segments &#x2014; refining, renewable diesel, and ethanol. Each segment is a strategic business unit that offers different products and services by employing unique technologies and marketing strategies and whose operations and operating performance are managed and evaluated separately. Operating performance is measured based on the operating income generated by the segment, which includes revenues and expenses that are directly attributable to the management of the respective segment. Intersegment sales are generally derived from transactions made at prevailing market rates. The following is a description of each segment&#x2019;s business operations.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;The &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;refining segment&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; includes the operations of our &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;15&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;petroleum refineries, the associated marketing activities, and logistics assets that support our refining operations. measurements are as follows:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Commodity derivative contracts consist primarily of exchange-traded futures, which are used to reduce the impact of price volatility on our results of operations and cash flows as discussed in &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;15&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;. These contracts are measured at fair value using a market approach based on quoted prices from the commodity exchange and are categorized in Level&#160;1 of the fair value hierarchy.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Physical purchase contracts represent the fair value of fixed-price corn purchase contracts. The fair values of these purchase contracts are measured using a market approach based on quoted prices from the commodity exchange or an independent pricing service and are categorized in Level&#160;2 of the fair value hierarchy.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Investments of certain benefit plans consist of investment securities held by trusts for the purpose of satisfying a portion of our obligations under certain U.S. nonqualified benefit plans. The plan assets categorized in Level&#160;1 of the fair value hierarchy are measured at fair value using a market approach based on quoted prices from national securities exchanges. The plan assets categorized in Level&#160;3 of the fair value hierarchy represent insurance contracts, the fair value of which is provided by the insurer.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Foreign currency contracts consist of foreign currency exchange and purchase contracts and foreign currency swap agreements related to our international operations to manage our exposure to exchange rate fluctuations on transactions denominated in currencies other than the local (functional) currencies of our operations. These contracts are valued based on quoted foreign currency exchange rates and are categorized in Level&#160;1 of the fair value hierarchy.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Environmental credit obligations represent our liability for the purchase of (i)&#160;biofuel credits (primarily Renewable Identification Numbers (RINs) in the U.S.) needed to satisfy our obligation to blend biofuels into the products we produce and (ii)&#160;emission credits under the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;California Global Warming Solutions Act&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; (the California cap-and-trade system, also known as AB&#160;32) and similar programs (collectively, the cap-and-trade systems). To the degree we are unable to blend biofuels (such as ethanol and biodiesel) at percentages required under the biofuel programs, we must purchase biofuel credits to comply with these programs. Under the cap-and-trade systems, we must purchase emission credits to comply with these systems. The liability for environmental credits is based on our deficit for such credits as of the balance sheet date, if any, after considering any credits acquired or under contract, and is equal to the product of the credits deficit and the market price of these credits as of the balance sheet date. The environmental credit obligations are categorized in Level&#160;2 of the fair value hierarchy and are measured at fair value using a market approach based on quoted prices from an independent pricing service.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span We enter into derivative instruments to manage some of these risks, including derivative instruments related to the various commodities we purchase or produce, and foreign currency exchange and purchase contracts, as described below under &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;&#x201c;Risk Management Activities by Type of Risk.&#x201d;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; These derivative instruments are recorded as either assets or liabilities measured at their fair values (see &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;14&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;), as summarized below under &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;&#x201c;Fair Values of Derivative Instruments.&#x201d;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; The effect of these derivative instruments on our income and other comprehensive income (loss) is summarized below under &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;&#x201c;Effect of Derivative Instruments on Income and Other Comprehensive Income (Loss).&#x201d;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Risk Management Activities by Type of Risk&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Commodity Price Risk&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We are exposed to market risks related to the volatility in the price of crude oil, refined petroleum products (primarily gasoline and distillate),&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#ee2724;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;renewable diesel, grain (primarily corn), renewable diesel feedstocks, and natural gas used in our operations. To reduce the impact of price volatility on our results of operations and cash flows, we use commodity derivative instruments, such as futures and options. Our positions in commodity derivative instruments are monitored and managed on a daily basis by our risk control group to ensure compliance with our stated risk management policy that has been approved by our board of directors.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We primarily use commodity derivative instruments as cash flow hedges and economic hedges. Our objectives for entering into each type of hedge is described below.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; The objective of our cash flow hedges is to lock in the price of forecasted&#160;(i)&#160;feedstock, refined petroleum product, or natural gas purchases, or&#160;(ii)&#160;refined petroleum product or renewable diesel sales at existing market prices that we deem favorable.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Economic hedges&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; &#x2013; Our objectives for holding economic hedges are to&#160;(i)&#160;manage price volatility in certain feedstock and refined petroleum product inventories and fixed-price purchase contracts, and&#160;(ii)&#160;lock in the price of forecasted feedstock, refined petroleum product,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#ff0000;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;or natural gas purchases, or refined petroleum product or renewable diesel sales at existing market prices that we deem favorable.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, we had the following outstanding commodity derivative instruments that were used as cash flow hedges and economic hedges, as well as commodity derivative instruments related to the physical purchase of corn at a fixed price. The information presents the notional volume of outstanding contracts by type of instrument and year of maturity (volumes in thousands of barrels, except corn contracts that are presented in thousands of bushels).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;padding-left:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;div style="vertical-align:bottom;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"&gt;&lt;div style="overflow:hidden;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:bottom;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:right;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;1,214&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:bottom;background-color:#cceeff;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Foreign Currency Risk&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We are exposed to exchange rate fluctuations on transactions related to our international operations that are denominated in currencies other than the local (functional) currencies of our operations. To manage our exposure to these exchange rate fluctuations, we use foreign currency contracts. These contracts are not designated as hedging instruments for accounting purposes and therefore are classified as economic hedges. As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, we had foreign currency contracts to purchase &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$219&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; of U.S. dollars, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$1.9&#160;billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; of U.S. dollar equivalent Canadian dollars, and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$500&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; of U.S. dollar equivalent pounds sterling. Of these commitments, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$919&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#ee2724;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;matured on or before &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;July&#160;24, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and the remaining &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$1.7&#160;billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; will mature by &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;October&#160;15, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Environmental Compliance Program Price Risk&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We are exposed to market risk related to the volatility in the price of credits needed to comply with various governmental and regulatory environmental compliance programs. To manage this risk, we enter into contracts to purchase these credits when prices are deemed favorable. Some of these contracts are derivative instruments; however, we elect the normal purchase exception and do not record these contracts at their fair values. Certain of these programs require us to blend biofuels into the products we produce, and we are subject to such programs in most of the countries in which we operate. These countries set annual quotas for the percentage of biofuels that must be blended into the motor fuels consumed in these countries. As a producer of motor fuels from petroleum, we are obligated to blend biofuels into the products we produce at a rate that is at least equal to the applicable quota. To the degree we are unable to blend at the applicable &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;rate, we must purchase biofuel credits (primarily RINs in the U.S.). We are exposed to the volatility in the market price of these credits, and we manage that risk by purchasing biofuel credits when prices are deemed favorable. The cost of meeting our obligations under these compliance programs was &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$136&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$67&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; for the three months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, respectively, and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$248&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$158&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; for the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, respectively. These amounts are reflected in cost of materials and other.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We are subject to additional requirements under greenhouse gas (GHG) emission programs, including the cap-and-trade systems, as discussed in &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Note&#160;14&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;. Under these cap-and-trade systems, we purchase various GHG emission credits available on the open market. Therefore, we are exposed to the volatility in the market price of these credits. The cost to implement certain provisions of the cap-and-trade systems are significant; however, we recovered the majority of these costs from our customers for the three and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and expect to continue to recover the majority of these costs in the future. For the three and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, the net cost of meeting our obligations under these compliance programs was immaterial.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Fair Values of Derivative Instruments&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;The following tables provide information about the fair values of our derivative instruments as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"&gt;December&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; (in&#160;millions) and the line items in the balance sheets in which the fair values are reflected. See &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Note&#160;14&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; for additional information related to the fair values of our derivative instruments.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;As indicated in &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Note&#160;14&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, we net fair value amounts recognized for multiple similar derivative contracts executed with the same counterparty under master netting arrangements, including cash collateral assets and obligations. Risk&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Our price risk management activities involve the receipt or payment of fixed price commitments into the future. These transactions give rise to market risk, which is the risk that future changes in market conditions may make an instrument less valuable. We closely monitor and manage our exposure to market risk on a daily basis in accordance with policies approved by our board of directors. Market risks are monitored by our risk control group to ensure compliance with our stated risk management policy. We do not require any collateral or other security to support derivative instruments into which we enter. We also do not have any derivative instruments that require us to maintain a minimum investment-grade credit rating.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div
